title: Compact scroll protocol and tenant-aware indexlet for low-memory dashboard pagination
creator: Lena Chen
description: Introduce a new lightweight pagination mode (Compact Scroll Protocol) plus a tenant-aware in-memory indexlet to reduce memory amplification and tail latency for large-dashboard queries. The goal is to handle long result sets (time series, large user lists, event logs) without full result materialization, reduce GC pressure on console backend workers, and keep per-tenant memory bounded while preserving low 95/99th percentile latency. This ticket covers design, runtime changes, index updater, API compatibility, and rollout strategy.
acceptance_criteria: API: /v1/dashboard/scroll supports ?mode=compact with stable opaque cursor and deterministic ordering for supported queries
Memory: per-worker memory footprint for heavy tenants reduced by >=35% in artifacted load tests compared to baseline
Latency: 95th and 99th percentile tail latency for paginated dashboard endpoints reduced by >=20% under skewed tenant load
Compatibility: old cursors (legacy mode) continue to work; compact mode falls back to legacy when indexlet unavailable
Observability: dashboards track compact-mode adoption, per-tenant cache hit rate, indexlet staleness, and rollback metrics
tech_notes: Compact Scroll Protocol: cursor encodes (tenant_id, indexlet_epoch, position_hint, checksum). Server uses position_hint to fetch a bounded slice from indexlet and streams results. Cursors are opaque to clients.

Indexlet: a memory-compact per-tenant shard of the global time-index containing (record_key, byte_offset, ordering_key) for recent N items. Implemented as a ring buffer of compressed entries plus a sparse lookup map; persisted to a small disk-backed LRU when evicted.

Write path changes: indexlet updated asynchronously on write path via background writer pipeline to avoid write latency amplification. Writes are batched per-tenant and flushed every ~150ms or when buffer exceeds threshold.

Consistency model: eventual within indexlet_epoch window. Queries hitting a slightly stale indexlet will be corrected by a short revalidation pass using a secondary quick scan over primary index (bounded to small window).
Resource trade-offs: reduces long-lived heap by avoiding materialized arrays; increases CPU for index maintenance and background flushes; introduces modest disk IO for evicted indexlets.
Compatibility: compact mode only for query shapes passing predicate analyzer (no ad-hoc arbitrary joins). Fallback to legacy cursor-based streaming for unsupported shapes.
rollout_plan: Stage 1: Internal rollout to staging cluster, run synthetic skewed-tenant load (1k tenants with power-law distribution)
Stage 2: Canary 5% production tenants (non-critical customers) and monitor memory, CPU, 95/99 latency and error rates for 72 hours
Stage 3: Ramp to 25% with continuous monitors and automated rollback if tail latency or errors regress beyond thresholds
Stage 4: Full rollout and enable default for new tenants after 2 weeks of stable metrics
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Indexlet staleness causing incorrect pagination or missing items. Mitigation: bounded revalidation pass and checksum in cursor to detect divergence; fall back to legacy stream if mismatch persists.
Risk: Increased CPU on metadata-heavy tenants. Mitigation: autoscale policies and throttling background flushes; ability to opt tenant out of compact mode.
Risk: Disk IO from evicted indexlets causing jitter. Mitigation: rate-limit background writes and use local SSD caches in dedicated nodes; monitor IOPS and add pressure-based eviction tuning.
Risk: Complexity in debugging cross-tenant ordering bugs. Mitigation: extensive integration tests and add per-tenant trace headers in logs to reconstruct pagination flows.
Risk: Client-side assumptions about cursor structure. Mitigation: keep cursor opaque and document that only server validations are guaranteed; ensure smooth fallback behavior.
testing_plan: Unit tests for cursor encoding/decoding and indexlet eviction/rehydration
Integration tests: legacy and compact modes produce identical result sequences for supported query shapes under concurrent writes
Load tests: simulate power-law tenant distribution with synthetic events; measure memory, 95/99 latency, and CPU across worker fleet
Chaos tests: kill background indexlet writer, simulate disk pressure, and validate fallback correctness
Observability tests: ensure metrics emitted (indexlet_epoch, hit_rate, revalidation_count, fallback_count) and dashboards update within 1m intervals
implementation_notes: Server changes: add CompactScrollHandler in console-query service; reuse existing query planner but short-circuit materialization for supported plans
Indexlet store: implement in console-index-worker component with protobuf wire format for compact entries
Backwards compatibility: maintain legacy Streamer codepath and share result serialization; add integration shim to translate legacy cursors
SDK changes: server-side only for now; clients remain unaffected (opaque cursors). Future SDK surface to expose mode flag for advanced users.
Instrumentation: add logs at DEBUG for first 100 compact-mode cursors per tenant to aid debugging during rollout
